name: Dobutamine
executiveSummary: Selective β1 inotrope. Adult/pediatrics: **2.5–20 mcg/kg/min** continuous IV (common max **40 mcg/kg/min**). NICU: **2–10 mcg/kg/min**. Do not use in dynamic LVOT obstruction.
indications:
## Indications

- Low output / decompensated HF / cardiogenic shock needing inotropy.
- Pharmacologic stress testing (different regimen).

## Precautions

- Tachycardia, arrhythmias, hypotension if vasodilation; contraindicated in dynamic LVOT obstruction.
- Incompatible with alkaline solutions.

> Titrate to cardiac index / MAP / lactate; central line preferred.

adulto.presentation: Ampule 12.5 mg/mL (20 mL = 250 mg) or institutional vial.
adulto.finalConcentration: E.g. **1000–2000 mcg/mL** (250–500 mg in 250 mL); common max **5 mg/mL**.
adulto.dose: **2.5–20 mcg/kg/min** continuous IV; titrate. Usual max **40 mcg/kg/min**.
adulto.notes: Slight pink color = mild oxidation without clear potency loss; discard if brown/precipitated.

pediatrico.dose: **2–20 mcg/kg/min** continuous IV; common max **40 mcg/kg/min**.
pediatrico.notes: Orient. compatible with dopamine, epinephrine, lidocaine (verify local guide). Dilution ~24 h.

stability:
## Stability

- Dilution: ~24 h. Protect from light per local guide.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Tachycardia, arrhythmias, hypotension, nausea, anxiety, myocardial ischemia.
